To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the neuropeptides from the B1 and B 2 neurons can be released in response to depolarization, that this release is inhibited by several physiologically active compounds, and that this inhibition is due to the ability of these compounds to elevate cAMP levels in the cells.
5-HT and FMRFamide depress the release of the neuropeptide SCPs in Aplysia B1 and B 2 cells.

(1) the neuropeptides of the B1 and B 2 cells can be released from single cells in culture in a stimulus- dependent fashion; and (2) the release of the B cell neuropeptides can be inhibited by the application of 5-HT and FMRFamide, but the mechanisms by which this occurs are not well understood.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of neuropeptides in the nervous system.
the mechanisms underlying the release of the neuropeptide, small cardioactive peptides A and B (SCPAs and SCPBs) from identified Aplysiae neurons.
the regulation of neuropeptide release.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

1) the release of the neuropeptide SCPs from single Aplysia sensory neurons is inhibited by several agonists, including 5-HT, 2) this inhibition of release is not due to a loss of spikes, and 3) the inhibition of release is probably not due to a hyperpolarized membrane potential, but rather may be due to an increase in the threshold of the release mechanism.
the release of the neuropeptide, SCPA from the B1 neuron is inhibited by 5-HT, which is mediated by a cAMP-dependent pathway.
the peptide release is inhibited by the agonists and that this inhibition is not correlated to a change in the membrane excitability of the cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found that 5HT and FMRFamide inhibit the release of the B cell peptides from single B cells in culture.
the effects of 5-HT on B1 and B 2 are opposite, and that the effect of 5-HT is to decrease the release of the B cell peptides.
the release of the neuropeptide, SCP, from the B1 and B 2 neurons is regulated in a cell-specific and agonist-specific fashion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
5HT and FMRFamide inhibit peptide release from B1 and B 2 cells in culture, and that this inhibition is not due to hyperpolarization and loss of spikes.
the effects of 5-HT and FMRFamide on the release of SCPs are not mediated by an alteration of the membrane potential of the cell body.
the neuropeptide SCPB can be released by single identified neurons in a stimulus-dependent fashion.
